clue.text: Talk foolishly of outing in car with trainee chauffeur

parts.note: a drive is a trip out in a car
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate on a British learner's car

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a ride out with a learner at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is nonsense, so as a verb it means to babble or prattle.

clue.text: Pale — right poorly

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: A remark that someone looks pale and quite unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like an adjective for a sick face, but it is the noun: a fence post or fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a stake or fence, and a railing is such a fence or barrier.

clue.text: Bunk put low in vessel

indicators.note: in tells us the cow's call is placed inside the container word

parts.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Someone's bed has been put down low inside a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed but is the British verb as in 'do a bunk': run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk off is slang for to flee, and vamoose is slang for clearing off quickly.

clue.text: Muslim set up space to sit comfortably

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a Moor is a Muslim of North Africa or medieval Spain
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A Muslim sets up a comfortable seating area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run MOORGEL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for the legs is what makes a seat comfortable, especially on a plane.

clue.text: China from Newcastle?

parts.note: porcelain from a Shropshire maker named after a place that shipped fuel; Newcastle is famous for shipping coal, so its harbour fits the description

explanation.surface: A question about where a piece of porcelain came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Coalport is a famous English porcelain maker; Newcastle upon Tyne was historically the great coal-shipping port, hence 'carrying coals to Newcastle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coalport is a brand of fine English porcelain, and china is porcelain.

clue.text: Unfashionable, more appropriate, attire supplied by him

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
fitter means more fitting, more suitable

explanation.surface: A man supplies clothes that are unfashionable but more suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or dealer that sells clothing.

clue.text: Feel anger, changing colour

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone whose face changes colour as they grow angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf-green is a shade of green like that of foliage.

clue.text: Newspaper, say, one singular editor ran

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group, a newspaper being an example
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sole editor was in charge of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' sits at the end looking like the editor's action, but it is the definition in the sense of managed.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an event is to arrange and manage it.

clue.text: System of betting is to alter drastically

indicators.note: drastically suggests a radical change, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants to overhaul a gambling system.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser is the tote, a pool betting system in which winners share the stakes.

clue.text: Established in business

explanation.definitionFit: Firm means fixed and secure, and also names a commercial company.

clue.text: Crook has got grit, to stop being a criminal

indicators.note: crook as a verb means to bend, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain shows the determination to give up crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' seems to be the villain but signals an anagram of HAS GOT GRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To go straight is the idiom for leaving a life of crime behind.

clue.text: Soldier taking turn, see, as professional escort

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a go is a turn in a game
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A soldier takes a turn as a paid companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to accompany or be the lover of a woman.

clue.text: Spotless keyboard instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Virginal means pure, and a virginal is a Tudor-era plucked keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Mere agent organised concert

indicators.note: organised means the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A mere agent arranged a musical concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concert' is not a performance but harmony of views, as in 'acting in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert in the sense of accord or unity of purpose is agreement.

clue.text: Confession from schoolgirl, one kept in by a member of teaching staff

indicators.note: kept in by means the girl and the numeral are held inside the teacher's letters, as in detention

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
miss is a word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl's confession after a teacher keeps her in detention.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a girl in detention; 'from' is only a link, and a don is a British university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement of a fault, a confession.

clue.text: Bird killed in the air — rook, caught by violent creature

annotationWithheld.why: Bird killed in the air - rook, caught by violent creature (9): R inside BEAST gives BREAST, but nothing found turns 'killed in the air' into RED; scan reads the same, and searches gave no parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Bird killed in the air — rook, caught by violent creature

clue.text: Found his table's incorrect

indicators.note: incorrect says these letters are wrongly ordered and must be put right

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a man's table is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but is the verb meaning to set up; 'incorrect' rearranges HIS TABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up from scratch.

clue.text: Key city — it rises, overlooking a lake

indicators.note: in a down clue overlooking places these letters below the ones above

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the little word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A key city stands on a rise above a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Key as an adjective means crucial, indispensable.

clue.text: Relaxes, having taken part in quite a session

indicators.note: taken part in says the answer is a part held within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds after joining a long session.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or slacken, and relaxes means the same.

clue.text: Two ways to capture damsel's head and heart

indicators.note: to capture means the letter is taken inside the two road words

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
ST is short for street, another way

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of damsel's

explanation.surface: Two methods of winning a young woman's mind and affections.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, so the clue's 'way' can be a road number.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre, its middle.

clue.text: He hopes the way he plays will please partner

definitions.text: He hopes the way he plays will please partner

parts.words: He hopes the way he plays will please partner
parts.note: a man performing love songs under a window, hoping his music wins his sweetheart

explanation.surface: A musician hoping his performance pleases his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partner' suggests a bridge or tennis player, but the player is a musician wooing a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sings or plays outdoors at night to a beloved hopes to charm her.

clue.text: Mission shut in vessel's inside

indicators.note: inside places the ship's letters within the enclosing word

parts.note: to embay is to enclose or shut in, as within a bay
SS is a steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A mission is confined within a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut in' looks like part of the surface's confinement picture, but it is one rare verb, to enclose as in a bay.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission to a foreign country.

clue.text: Hopin' for a remedy

definitions.meaning: aspiring with the final g dropped means hoping

explanation.surface: Someone is hoping for a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Hopin'' tells you to drop the G of a word meaning hoping.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller, and aspiring means hoping.

clue.text: Various directions, one repeated, are needed to make trap

parts.note: compass points E, N, S, with north given twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several directions are needed to lay a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a snare, to trap.

clue.text: In his natural habitat. Bedouin, say, presents dance

indicators.note: In places the desert dweller inside the word for his home terrain

parts.note: sand, the desert, is the Bedouin's natural home
a Bedouin is an example of an Arab

explanation.surface: A desert nomad at home performs a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his natural habitat' looks ahead to Bedouin: the desert, here SAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance.

clue.text: Go round through gap

parts.note: by means via or through
a pass is a gap through mountains

explanation.surface: A traveller goes round by a mountain gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass is to go around something rather than through it.

clue.text: In such fantasies, I am opposed to illicit groups deposing king

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
agin is dialect for against

indicators.note: deposing means the king's letter is removed from the gang word

parts.note: rings are illegal networks, as in drug rings
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A fantasist opposes criminal gangs who overthrow a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasies are things dreamt up in the mind, flights of imagination.

clue.text: Wander round in force

indicators.note: in tells us the ring shape goes inside the word for force

parts.note: to ram is to force
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: People wander about in force.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander without fixed course.

clue.text: Given bananas, he will produce packaging for fruit

parts.note: bananas and nuts both mean crazy
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: A man handed bananas makes wrapping for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit, but is the slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut's hard case is the natural packaging around the kernel, a fruit.

clue.text: Bet he's a Northerner

definitions.meaning: a multiple wager of four selections in eleven combined bets
an American from the northern states, as in the Civil War

explanation.definitionFit: A yankee is both a British accumulator wager and a native of the northern USA.
